user_scenario: You are Theodora Haraldsen, 55, a school librarian in Marblehead, Massachusetts, a Larkspur Premier member who gets her blood pressure pill, olmesartan, mailed by Larkspur Pharmacy as a 90-day supply. You are calm, organised and a little apologetic about taking up time. You open by saying that your October refill of the olmesartan, the one that came overnight, was charged a different amount than your earlier 90-day refills, that you want to settle whatever you actually still owe on that October order today, and that you would like to pay it yourself with your HSA card, which is not the card Larkspur has on file. You do not know the right amount and never suggest one. Only when the agent asks for identifying details do you give them, one or two at a time: your Larkspur patient number is LH-8330417 and your date of birth is May 19, 1971 (1971-05-19); if a further detail is needed, your mobile is 6175550143 and your home ZIP code is 01945. If the agent asks which order you mean, it is the 90-day olmesartan refill that shipped on October 9th. If the agent explains that something else on your pharmacy account has to be corrected or refunded first, you say that is fine and to go ahead, without asking for details. If the agent offers to charge the card on file instead, you say you would rather use the HSA card for your medication. Once the agent tells you the amount and hands the payment step over to you, you make that payment yourself for exactly the quoted amount on the October order. When the agent confirms the payment went through, you thank them and say goodbye.

design_rationale:
WHY A GOOD TEST: Theodora Haraldsen (Premier Annual, active) asks only to settle what she still owes on her October 9 olmesartan 90-day refill and to pay it with an HSA card not on file. The answer (4.20) is hidden behind two corrections the policy imposes first and a whole-shipment re-pricing with six factors: the agent must read the shipment-balance rule's two prerequisite sentences, find in the billing lines that the October shipping line (42.40) stands above the allowed shipping fee (32.45) and that the July 16 benefit-basis line (96.40) stands above the lesser of its pbm (96.40) and the member cash price (63.00), book both refunds, then price the October shipment and net it against what remains collected. Difficulty comes from reading policy and records and calculating, not from guessing tools.
SCOPE: task 0 claims rx_ext_benefit_line_refund, rx_ext_shipping_overcharge_refund, rx_ext_cash_shipment_balance and their three tools (cash_member_price and pbm-basis shipments); task 1 keeps the cash_price-basis shipment pair (owed shipping paid by the patient, then the net shipment refund) — disjoint.
DRAW: prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[6,5,5] -> balance 6, shipping refund 5, benefit-line refund 5.
PROBLEM TREE: root rx_ext_cash_shipment_balance (user, pay_rx_shipment_balance_955e5801). Edge 1 value_input, state form, gate `collected`: 'The shipment balance is fixed only after the shipment's shipping line, plus every refund line pointing at it, stands no higher than the shipping fee the shipment balance allows.' False at opening: initial_state.rx_charges.1831acda-b499-42da-ab22-c6922dae0982.amount=42.4 with no refund; resolved by refund_rx_shipping_overcharge_36ef431c (agent) booking 9.95. Edge 2 state_gate, state form, gate rx_charges.original_charge_id: 'The shipment balance is not collected until every fill charge line of the same prescription posted on the pharmacy-benefit basis above the lesser of its recorded pbm patient pay and its member cash price carries a billing-error refund.' False at opening: initial_state.rx_charges.87597c57-70ad-4c36-a022-be52d8047cc9.price_basis=pbm_patient_pay, amount 96.4, no refund; resolved by refund_rx_benefit_line_87d0f93d (agent) booking 33.40. Topological order E5, E3, E4 (E5/E3 commute: different fills and lines; run either order -> 33.40, 9.95, 4.20). Deletion sensitivity: skip E3 -> balance 0.00 instead of 4.20 (collected 101.20 vs allowed 95.45); skip E5 -> refund row missing. user_scenario names no correction, refund, July order or insurance; tools validate no prerequisite.
FACTOR CARD (handling-time recomputation, scratch evaluator over the gate's own primitives): balance 4.20 = (63.00 drug + 32.45 shipping) - 91.25 collected; member_percent Premier 25 on Extended Generics (baseline 25.20), premier_speed_waiver overnight 24.95-9.95 (14.15), peak_season_surcharge 3.50 for 2026-10-09 inside 2026-10-01..2027-01-15 (0.70), weekend_transit_fee 8.00 Friday overnight (0.00), ninety_day_parcel 4.00 (0.20), package_protection 1.95 on 58.80 posted (2.25); all-baseline 17.70. Shipping refund 9.95 (premier 0.00, peak 13.45, weekend 17.95, parcel 13.95, protection 11.90; all-baseline 17.45). Benefit-line refund 33.40 = 104.35 - (63.00 + 7.95) (member 12.40, premier 23.45 expedited waived, weekend 37.40 Thursday expedited, parcel 35.40, protection 35.35; all-baseline 10.40). Cross-difficulty: membership_holdings Premier Annual active (multi-source tier AND status). Near-misses: January/April lines carry a pbm figure but sit on the cash member price basis (excluded from the benefit-line read); the July refund points at another fill and is excluded from the October collected amount; peak window excludes July.
BASE-INVARIANT CARD: refunds inherit rx_returns_and_reships.one_refund_per_line (no refund points at either line at opening); the balance line inherits rx_evt_fill_pricing charge_state (prescription completed: four 90-day fills used all 12 units), rx_member_discount_state (membership active) and benefit_coverage_verified (HDHP verified; the balance line is cash). Overwrites declared: rx_evt_shipping speed-fee sentence -> Larkspur shipping schedule with surcharges; rx_evt_fill_pricing 'charged once' -> a cash-member-price shipment below the rules is charged its balance as a second fill charge line; rx_returns_and_reships correction clause -> whole-shipment refund on pbm-basis lines of lower_of levels and cash_price-basis shipments.
BUSINESS OBJECTS: October 9 fill 60379781-96d5-4d1f-aae8-f6bde12d1076 (drug line 8abb1aa6-5425-45f4-ae0e-70a0a641bdca 58.80 at 30 percent instead of 25, shipping 1831acda-b499-42da-ab22-c6922dae0982 42.40); July 16 fill c40925c2-5cf2-450a-a384-8e2e6220b0a9 (drug 87597c57-70ad-4c36-a022-be52d8047cc9 96.40 pbm basis, shipping 7.95 correct). Every aggregate is keyed on rx_fill_id.
SEED: Premier Annual since 2025-03-12 (99.00 fee, 899.00 dues 2025 and 2026); January 20 completed Primary Care Follow-Up (membership_included, no charge) wrote the 90-day prescription; Jan/Apr fills priced correctly at 63.00 cash member price with pbm recorded; HDHP Keystone coverage verified. No automatic clause ignites another obligation.
PERSONA: calm librarian; volunteers the October order, the wish to settle it and the HSA card; identity only when asked; agrees to other corrections only after the agent raises them; pays exactly the quoted amount when handed the payment step.
SOLUTION: find_customers -> verify -> prescriptions, fills, charges, membership, membership charges, coverage, visit -> refund 33.40 on the July line -> refund 9.95 on the October shipping line -> hand over payment of 4.20 on the October fill.
